name: Telamont
long_description:
Telamont catches contractual, technical and code-compliance risks in construction documents and gives teams the system to act on them before they become costly rework or disputes.

Construction projects lose money in the gap between what the documents say and what gets built. One missed discrepancy between the specs, drawings, geotechnical study and code can become a seven-figure claim eighteen months later.

Telamont connects to where your documents live and pulls in every file and revision as it lands, continuously building a complete picture of the project. Every page is checked against the rest of the project, so risks are flagged as soon as they appear. Instead of reviewing documents, teams act on flagged risks, tracking each from detection to resolution while managing exposure and pursuing recovery opportunities across every project.
one_liner: Sentry for errors in construction documents

launches.title: Telamont — Sentry for errors in construction documents
launches.tagline: AI that catches errors between construction drawings, specs and contracts
launches.body:
Hey YC! I'm Charles, and my co-founder William and I are building Telamont.\
\
**TL;DR:** Telamont catches the errors hiding between construction drawings, specs and contracts, before they become disputes. We protect $2B+ of construction today, and we'd love intros to builders.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QakQbKSmLAc>

**The Problem**

My grandpa built dams. My dad builds bridges. At the dinner table, they sounded more like attorneys than builders. Their stories were almost always about disputes, and most of them started in the documents.

That's not just my family. The average construction dispute in North America costs $60.1M, and the #1 cause is errors and omissions in contract documents (Source: [Arcadis, 2025 Construction Disputes Report](https://www.arcadis.com/en-us/expertise/contract-solutions)).

On a big project, thousands of drawings, specs and contracts are written by different firms. Every document gets reviewed, but no one reviews how they fit together.

A note on one sheet changes the price. A detail on another doesn't match the structure. A clause in a subcontract moves the cost to someone else.

These usually surface in the field. By then, it's a fight over who pays.

**How Telamont works**

1. Telamont connects to where your documents already live, like SharePoint, Dropbox or Autodesk. Every new file is pulled in as it lands and checked against the rest of the project. You don't have to upload anything or start a review.
2. When something doesn't line up, Telamont flags it with the exact sheets and clauses that conflict, so your team can act on it in minutes.
3. Sometimes it’s a risk, money you’re owed, or a change order opportunity. Each one gets an owner and is tracked from detection to resolution, across every project.

\
**What Telamont catches**

* **$450K owed:** one note in the construction set upgraded 30 light poles to a model twice the price. No addendum, no revision cloud.
* **$1.1M of foundation rework avoided:** the structural drawings designed footings for twice the soil capacity the geotechnical report allowed.
* **$400K of missing structure:** the architect showed an elevator and stair tower, but the structural plans had no pit or openings.
* **Crane scope mismatch:** a sub bid its crane for its own work, but the subcontract made it hoist for every trade.

**The team**

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=126833&key=user_uploads/3119151/acbdfe41-6e95-4f38-87bf-a0654c278af2)

I'm the third generation of a construction family, and I was a software engineer at 1Password before starting Telamont.

William, my co-founder and CTO, previously applied AI to manufacturing operations as a software engineer at Poka. We started our first business together in high school, building longboards.

Our four early hires include people from WSP and AtkinsRéalis, two of the world's largest engineering firms.

\
**The ask: Intros to builders**

If you know anyone who works at a general contractor, a quick “you should talk to Charles” text would mean the world. Construction runs on relationships and warm intros are everything. 

If you build, design or own complex construction projects, [book a demo](https://telamont.com/launch) or email us at [founders@telamont.com](mailto:founders@telamont.com).

My family spent three generations fighting disputes after the fact. We’re building the tool that lets the next generation prevent them.
